terms.definition: The over-saturated, over-smooth, plasticky signature of raw generative output; killed in post with grain, aberration, and desaturation.
Widescreen lens aesthetic with horizontal flares and oval bokeh; a common prompt tag for cinematic feel.
Frame proportions (16:9, 21:9, 9:16, 1:1); choose before generating, post-cropping destroys composition.
The aesthetic quality of out-of-focus areas; shallow depth of field renders backgrounds as soft bokeh.
The virtual camera's trajectory through a shot (dolly, orbit, crane); described in prompts or set via camera controls.
Higgsfield's node-graph workspace connecting generation, transformation, and editing steps; graph edits are free.
Traditional hand-drawn 2D style (one drawing per cel); prompt register for anime work (sakuga, held frames, smears).
Composite reference image showing a character from multiple angles (front/side/3-4) used to lock identity.
High-contrast light/shadow lighting style; a reliable dramatic prompt descriptor.
Color fringing at high-contrast edges; added in post to mimic real lens physics.
Higgsfield's directing surface: prompt + camera presets, genres, eras, AI cast, grading, multi-reference, co-directing.
Stop-motion animation with clay figures; AI-achieved via style tags (Aardman/Laika look, fingerprints, stepped motion).
Shooting a scene from multiple angles (wide, close-ups, reverse shots); in AI, generated as separate consistent clips.
A shot that cuts away from the main action (e.g. an insert) to compress time or add information.
Decibels true peak; mastering ceiling is -1 dBTP so codecs don't clip inter-sample peaks.
Range of the shot in focus; "shallow DOF" isolates subjects, "deep focus" keeps everything sharp.
Identity/appearance shifting across generations; countered with trained IDs, reference sheets, re-anchoring.
Tilted camera framing that creates unease; a named compositional preset.
Higgsfield's reference system (@ Elements): characters, uploads, and past generations addressable in prompts.
Analog texture overlay; the fastest way to make AI footage feel photographed rather than rendered.
Generation mode that interpolates between a start and end image; used for transitions and match cuts.
Performed sound effects (footsteps, cloth, props) recorded or layered to match on-screen action.
Higgsfield tool: Motion Transfer or Object Swap on 3 to 30s source video while keeping camera motion/VFX.
The warm light around sunrise/sunset; the most-used cinematic lighting descriptor.
Higgsfield's voice suite: Voiceover, Change Voice, Translate (multilingual lip sync).
Animating a still image; the still is an anchor, describe evolution, not a new scene.
Prompt section holding only static visual descriptors (face, wardrobe, palette); no motion or camera language.
A close-up shot of a detail (hands, object, screen) cut into a scene.
Audio of the next shot enters before its picture; masks AI shot transitions.
A defining still (start, end, or story beat) that generations interpolate between or animate from.
Audio of the current shot lingers over the next shot's picture; masks AI shot transitions.
Matching mouth movement to dialogue; done natively in-video (quoted dialogue) or as a post pass (Kling/Pika/Higgsfield tools).
A completely static camera shot; the correct prompt term (never "the camera doesn't move").
Loudness Units Full Scale; streaming target is -14 LUFS integrated for YouTube/Spotify, -23/-24 for broadcast.
Look-Up Table; a reusable color-grade preset applied across clips for unified color.
Music and Effects mix (dialogue removed); required for dubbing/localization deliverables.
Higgsfield's ad surface: URL-to-video, UGC talking heads, speech+lip-sync+product-lock packages.
A transition joining two shots via matched motion, shape, or composition.
A collection of reference images locking a project's visual direction before generation.
Prompt section holding only temporal/camera language; no character-appearance repetition.
Transferring motion from a reference video onto a generated character (Kling's "digital puppetry").
Generating several labeled shots (Shot 1/2/3) in one call; one action + one camera move per shot.
Sound generated alongside the video by the model (dialogue, SFX, ambience); prompted via quoted dialogue and named sounds.
Exclusion input; supported on some models (Veo, Pika, Wan) but backfires on others (Runway, Seedance, use compositional exclusion instead).
Seedance/Higgsfield mode using multiple reference inputs in one generation.
Oil-painting-style motion (impasto, brushstrokes, canvas texture); a stylized animation register.
Vertical camera move (up/down) with the body rising; distinct from crane (arm) and tilt (rotation).
Live-action-look output aiming to be indistinguishable from filmed footage.
Visible on-set light sources (lamps, signs, fluorescents) that motivate the scene's lighting.
How faithfully a model follows the prompt; tested per model and improved by specificity.
Automatic rewriting/enrichment of short prompts (e.g. Wan's prompt_extend, Gemini enhancement); disable for precise control.
Shifting focus between foreground and background mid-shot; a named lens-internal move.
Cutting the story to work as pure audio first, then cutting picture to the audio.
Sora 2's branching feature: vary action/subject while keeping style keywords identical for consistent series.
The ambient sound of a location; layered under dialogue to glue cuts together.
High-energy, fluidly animated cuts in anime; a style keyword for dynamic anime action.
The random seed returned per generation; stabilizes but does not lock output, reusing it reduces variance.
Reusing a seed across generations to hold composition/style steadier (a stabilizer, not a guarantee).
The approved generations kept for the edit; everything else is discarded, never upscaled.
Alternating over-the-shoulder framings of two speakers; the standard dialogue coverage pattern.
The planned sequence of shots with framing, movement, and action per shot; the AI director's shooting plan.
Higgsfield's AI-actor casting system: archetype-based consistent cinematic characters.
Higgsfield's cinematic image model: film grain, rich textures, movie-still compositions.
Higgsfield's color-lock system: extracts palettes from references and holds them across generations.
Higgsfield's trained identity layer: 20 to 80 photos → reusable face across the Soul family and Seedance.
Separated mix layers (dialogue, music, effects); kept separable for M&E deliverables.
Animation from individually posed frames; AI-approximated with stepped-motion and handmade-texture cues.
The single locked style description reused verbatim in every prompt of a project.
Higgsfield's agent surface: brief in plain language → it plans steps, picks models, shows cost, executes on approval.
Generating video from a text prompt alone; needs full scene description (40 to 100 words optimal on Runway).
Compressed-time effect; requires a static camera in AI generation.
Camera moving alongside or behind a subject, matching its pace.
Lateral camera move left/right (body slides); distinct from pan (rotation).
Lower-cost, faster, lower-fidelity model variants; often without native audio.
The discomfort zone where near-photoreal faces read as wrong; the main risk of the photoreal track.
Increasing resolution in post (e.g. Topaz Video AI to 4K); done only on final selects.
Post fixes: face replacement, artifact removal, added shake/grain to sell the shot.
Visible light shafts through haze/dust (god rays); a strong cinematic descriptor.
A fast blurred pan used as an energetic transition between shots.
